book.jugcraft.arcane_concordance.alembic:
Once you understand First Light, look closely at what things are made of. **Sneak and use** one of these to examine it:\
- Sugar\
- Sweet Berries\
- Dried Kelp\
- Spider Eye\
- Bone Meal\
- Honeycomb
Study one at a **Lampwright's Bench**, or read someone's **Research Notes**.
You can now work an **Alembic Crucible**. To **master** the Alembic Arts, bottle 3 different outcomes.
Your Assay Glass now tells you what a dose would do, and why.
Pour in water (a water bucket is 3 parts; at most 6), then use ingredients on it. Bottle with a glass bottle (a draught) or a bowl (a salve).

The crucible takes the heat of what is beneath it: magma 60, a campfire 120, fire 175, lava 220 degrees (nothing: 20). It warms or cools one degree a tick.\
\
**Cold** below 40 (10% a stir), **Warm** from 40 (30% a stir), **Hot** from 90 (55% a stir), **Searing** from 160 (80% a stir).

Ingredients do not dissolve by themselves. Each **stir** (a Stirring Rod or a stick) dissolves a share of what is still pending, more the hotter it is. But a **searing** stir keeps only 85% of the dissolved Radiance and Verdance and fouls the mixture.
A bottle takes one part's share of everything dissolved: that is its dose. The same process always makes the same mixture, so a good one can be made again.
Recording a process, and repeating it
Use a blank formula on a crucible to write down its whole process (water, every ingredient and how it was prepared, every stir and how hot) while nothing has been drawn from it.

Use a written formula on a crucible to set it (**sneak** with an empty hand to clear it). Fed water through a pipe and ingredients through a hopper (up to 5 kinds waiting), it follows the formula step by step, waiting for the heat each stir needs, and bottles into its output when it has bottles. A Pneumatic Extractor at its side takes the brews out, so the fire can stay beneath. It never guesses: a missing ingredient or the wrong heat simply waits.
What ingredients carry, and what it does

- Glowstone Dust: radiance 1.50\
- Glow Berries: radiance 0.60, verdance 0.60\
- Sweet Berries: verdance 1.00\
- Bone Meal: verdance 0.80, hollow 0.30 (contaminant 0.20)\
- Sugar: ember 0.90, tide 0.20\
- Magma Cream: ember 1.60 (contaminant 0.20)\
- Snowball: rime 1.00\
- Amethyst Shard: rime 0.80, radiance 0.40\
- Dried Kelp: tide 1.20\
- Honeycomb: tide 0.60, verdance 0.40\
- Spider Eye: hollow 1.20 (contaminant 0.30)\
- Sunpetal: radiance 1.00, verdance 0.60\
- Dewmoss: tide 1.40, verdance 0.30\
- Gloamcap: hollow 0.90, rime 0.40 (contaminant 0.10)\
- Mendvetch: verdance 1.40

- Radiance: Night Vision from 0.50 a part, 60 s a unit (at most 120 s)\
- Verdance: Regeneration from 0.60 a part, 15 s a unit (at most 22.5 s)\
- Ember: Fire Resistance from 0.60 a part, 60 s a unit (at most 120 s)\
- Rime: Resistance from 0.80 a part, 30 s a unit (at most 60 s)\
- Tide: Water Breathing from 0.60 a part, 60 s a unit (at most 120 s)\
- Hollow: Poison from 0.40 a part, 10 s a unit (at most 21.6 s)\
- Contaminant: Nausea from 0.50 a part, 8 s a unit (at most 20 s)\
\
A dose below a threshold does nothing for that property; too much contaminant brings nausea.
Used as it comes, an ingredient waits to be stirred out. **Ground** in a Mortar and Pestle it loses a tenth, but most of it dissolves the moment it goes in.
Knowing what is in the pot
Tells you how hot the mixture is, how much there is, which property is strongest and whether it is murky.

Measures every property, dissolved and pending, and the contaminant, a part at a time. Once you have mastered the Alembic Arts it also says what a dose would do and why: which property, how strong against its threshold, and which ingredients put it there.
book.jugcraft.arcane_concordance.artific: Rings forged, reforged, inscribed, socketed and bonded
What each process keeps and destroys

Hold the ring in your main hand and use the bench with, in your other hand: nothing (inspect it); redstone (**reforge**, 6 Focus); a rune's ingredient (**inscribe**, 4 Focus); a gem (**socket**); shears (**unsocket** the last gem); its substrate's ingot (**repair**); a lead (**bond** it to you, 10 Focus, or unbond it); flint (**salvage**, used twice to confirm).

- **Forge**: a new ring: substrate, quality and affixes rolled once\
- **Reforge**: keeps substrate, quality, runes, gems, bond and wear; new affixes\
- **Inscribe**: keeps everything; adds a rune\
- **Socket**: keeps everything; sets a gem\
- **Unsocket**: keeps everything but the last gem, which comes back whole\
- **Bond**: keeps everything; the ring serves only you, with one more capacity\
- **Unbond**: keeps everything but the bond\
- **Repair**: keeps everything; mends wear\
- **Salvage**: gives back some substrate and every gem; destroys quality, affixes, runes and bond

- **Amethyst** (amethyst shard): capacity 2\
- **Emerald** (emerald): capacity 1\
- **Diamond** (diamond): capacity 2\
- **Lapis** (lapis lazuli): capacity 1\
- **Quartz** (quartz): capacity 1

- **Rune of Radiance** (glowstone dust): capacity 2\
- **Rune of Swiftness** (sugar): capacity 2\
- **Rune of Warding** (obsidian): capacity 3\
- **Rune of Vigor** (golden carrot): capacity 2
Wear the ring in a **ring slot**. It wears one point every 30 seconds worn; at its last point it is **dull** and gives nothing until repaired, but it never breaks. A bonded ring serves only its bond.
Use it with ingots in hand to **forge** a Resonant Ring (8 Focus). Its quality and affixes are rolled once, on the server, and kept on the ring; you see them after they are made.

- **Copper**: 4 ingot(s), capacity 4, 1 socket(s), 1 rune slot(s); salvage gives back 2\
- **Iron**: 4 ingot(s), capacity 5, 1 socket(s), 1 rune slot(s); salvage gives back 2\
- **Gold**: 4 ingot(s), capacity 7, 2 socket(s), 2 rune slot(s); salvage gives back 2\
- **Netherite**: 1 ingot(s), capacity 9, 3 socket(s), 2 rune slot(s); salvage gives back 0
A ring's capacity is its substrate's, plus its quality (crude -1, sound 0, fine +1, masterwork +2), plus 1 while bonded. Affixes, runes and gems use it; nothing goes beyond it.

Once you understand First Light, look closely at smithing stock. **Sneak and use** one of these to examine it:\

Study one at a **Lampwright's Bench**, or read someone's **Research Notes**. To **master** Runesmithing, enhance rings in three different ways.
book.jugcraft.arcane_concordance.binding:
Once you understand First Light, look closely at what binds one thing to another. **Sneak and use** one of these to examine it:\
- Lead\
- Name Tag\
- Soul Lantern\
- Saddle\
- Echo Shard
Study one at a **Lampwright's Bench**, or read someone's **Research Notes**.
A familiar, a spirit and a construct will answer you now. To **master** the Binding Arts, be served by each once: a familiar's mending, a spirit's delivery and a construct's trip.
You keep many, and each keeps its own terms.

Unfold it on a block. Use a **Porter Key** on two containers (its source and its target), then on the porter. It carries 16 items a trip, spends 2 Ley Charge a trip (it holds 64, drawn from a Ley Pylon by its source that you may use) and wears 1 of its 64 integrity; each copper ingot mends 16.

Use the post with an item in your hand to **request** a stack of exactly that item (a named or enchanted one is not a plain one). Bind a Porter Key to the post, then use the key on a Clockwork Porter: it serves the post, fetching from containers within 8 blocks into the post's 9 slots (a hopper below takes them out).

One courier takes a request at a time and **reserves** what it will carry, so two never reach for the same items. What a courier has picked up is held by the post's ledger, not by the courier: if it is broken, unloaded or the world restarts, its cargo waits at the post for another courier, or for you (**/jugcraft concordance logistics recover**). A full post keeps the rest in transit; a cancelled request, or one whose post is broken, takes its cargo back first.

Use the post with an empty hand to read its last steps. **/jugcraft concordance logistics** lists your requests; **request** asks for a number of what you hold; **cancel** and **recover** take a request's number:\
- **open**: waiting for a courier\
- **claimed**: a courier is on it\
- **in transit**: in transit\
- **stranded**: stranded at the post (its courier is gone)\
- **returning**: being taken back
Familiars, spirits and constructs: bonds, agreements and bodies
Use it to bind a **Hearthling**: one familiar a person. It keeps within 8 blocks of you and, when you are badly hurt, mends you. Use the charm again to call it to your side; sneak to release it.

The bond grows by time spent together, 1 a visit and at most 24 a day, and fades by 4 for each day you are online but away from it. At 20 it mends you (at most once a minute); at 60, twice as often. It never follows you into another dimension and never waits in a place that is not loaded: it simply waits where it is.
What a worker can tell you

Look at a worker (Jade), use it with an empty hand, or ask **/jugcraft concordance workers** (which also lists workers that are not loaded, with what they last said):\
- **following**: following its person\
- **supporting**: mending its person\
- **travelling**: on its way\
- **working**: working\
- **returning**: taking what it carries home\
- **idle**: idle: nothing to do\
- **waiting for resources**: waiting for resources (its source is empty or gone)\

The Circlewrights' practice: rituals, their circles and their risks
A ritual is worked at a **Circle Anchor**, inside a circle built round it.

With the anchor at the centre:\
- a **Ley Pylon** two blocks out to the north, south, east and west (the **channels**);\
- a **Warding Stone** three blocks out in those four directions and two out on each diagonal (the **boundary**);\
- two blocks of **open air** above the anchor.\
\
All on the anchor's level. It works built facing any way.

Use the anchor with an empty hand to hear what is wrong: a part **missing**, the **wrong block**, the space **obstructed**, a pylon **without charge** or **someone else's**, or part of it **out of reach** (an unloaded chunk). Jade shows the first faults at a glance, and `/jugcraft concordance circle` reads the whole circle.
Any block in the ritual boundary tag will hold; these are made for it.
A pylon holds up to 64 **Ley Charge**, the working energy rituals draw. Each step of a ritual draws from every pylon in the circle at once, all or none.

**From a Kindled Lantern:** use the lantern on the pylon. Every 3 Radiance becomes 2 Ley Charge, up to 15 Radiance a pour; what does not convert stays in the lantern.\
\
**From electricity:** connect any Jugcraft power source. Every 1000 JE becomes 1 Ley Charge, at up to 64 JE a tick.\
\
Nothing turns Ley Charge back.
The pylon belongs to whoever placed it. A ritual draws only from pylons owned by someone taking part (or by no one).

Two practitioners keep a vigil in the dark: each is shielded, and creatures nearby are outlined.\
\
**Offer:** 4 Glow Berries.\
**Takes:** 2 practitioners, 4 Focus each, 3 steps (6 seconds), drawing 1 Ley Charge from each pylon a step (12 in all). It must be dark: light 7 or less above the anchor.
Each participant gains 8 points of absorption for 2 minutes, and up to 16 creatures within 16 blocks glow for a minute. It needs two people, but nothing else in the Concordance needs it.
What a ritual takes, and what it risks

Put the **offerings** in the anchor (use it with each). Then use it with an **empty hand**: the anchor finds the ritual the offerings answer, checks the circle, and takes your **Focus**. A ritual for more than one waits 30 seconds for the others, who join the same way. **Sneak** with an empty hand to take your offerings back before it begins.

Every 2 seconds the ritual checks the whole circle again and draws Ley Charge. Every participant must stay within 4 blocks of the circle's edge. The offerings are **held**: nothing can be added or taken until it ends. The leader can call it off by sneaking with an empty hand.

**Completed:** the offerings are used and the result is made, both at the same moment, once.\
\
**Broken off** (a part broken, a pylon dry, someone gone, too bright, the anchor's chunk unloaded or the server restarted): nothing is made, the offerings stay in the anchor for you to take back or try again, and the Focus and Ley Charge already spent are gone.

If a **Warding Stone** is lost while a ritual runs, the working lashes out: every participant takes its backlash. The offerings are still returned. If the anchor itself is broken, they drop where it stood.

A spell is a few words in order: a **delivery** (how it leaves you), a **selection** (what it chooses where it lands), one to 3 **operations** (what it does) and an optional **ending**. Join a **modifier** to the word it changes with **+**, and write **then** before a second spell that starts where the first landed.

Hold an instrument and type `/jugcraft concordance compose check` and the spell to see what it does and costs, or exactly why it cannot work. `compose inscribe` writes it on the instrument and it appears on your spell bar; `compose show` reads it back and `compose clear` wipes it.

- `touch struck light`: Light where you touch (2 Focus)\
- `here struck ward`: Ward yourself (3 Focus)\
- `ray struck sear then here creatures dazzle`: Sear what you aim at, then dazzle what stands round it (8 Focus)

The Initiate's Wand holds 8 capacity of words. A spell on it reaches at most 6 different targets, does at most 48 work, branches at most 1 time and lasts at most 60 seconds.\

A spell costs the Focus of its words (an operation's for every pulse), taken once when it takes effect: a spell that does nothing costs nothing. Its cooldown is half a second and a quarter second for each Focus, and lasts at least as long as it pulses.

`here`: The spell lands where you stand; after then, where the spell before it landed.\
\
No reach: it lands at once. Needs First Light understood. Capacity 1, Focus 0.

\
Reach: 16 blocks. Needs First Light mastered. Capacity 2, Focus 1.

\
3 times, every 1 seconds. Needs First Light mastered. Capacity 2, Focus 0.

`intensify`: Half as strong again (at least one more): joined to an operation.\
\
+50% strength. Needs First Light mastered. Capacity 1, Focus 2.

`prolong`: Twice as long: joined to an operation that lasts.\
\
+100% time. Needs First Light understood. Capacity 1, Focus 1.

+2 blocks radius. Needs First Light mastered. Capacity 1, Focus 2.

\
+8 blocks range. Needs First Light mastered. Capacity 1, Focus 1.

`light`: Sets a Kindled mote in open air you may build in.\
\
Lasts 32 seconds. Needs First Light understood. Capacity 1, Focus 2.

`reveal`: Makes a creature glow, seen through walls. Revealing another player counts as harming them.\
\
Lasts 10 seconds. Needs First Light understood. Capacity 1, Focus 1.

`ward`: A shell of light that absorbs harm (Absorption).\
\
Absorbs up to 4 damage for 10 seconds. Needs First Light understood. Capacity 2, Focus 3.

`sear`: Light that burns: arcane damage, credited to you.\

4 damage. Needs First Light mastered. Capacity 2, Focus 3.

`dazzle`: Dazzled creatures stumble (Slowness).\

Level 1 for 3 seconds. Needs First Light mastered. Capacity 1, Focus 2.

One target. Needs First Light understood. Capacity 0, Focus 0.

Up to 4 creatures within 3 blocks. Needs First Light mastered. Capacity 2, Focus 2.

Up to 4 blocks within 3 blocks. Needs First Light mastered. Capacity 2, Focus 2.

Up to 4 of you and your party within 4 blocks. Needs First Light mastered. Capacity 2, Focus 2.

The Starbound Conclave
Renown, ranks, commissions and shared projects
The Starbound Conclave

The Conclave is the fellowship of the Concordance's traditions, and its factions are those traditions: every research entry belongs to one. Once you understand First Light, use a **Conclave Lectern** (or **/jugcraft concordance conclave join**) to swear its oath. It replaces nothing: your party stays your party and Jugs stay the only coin. Renown is standing, never spent.
The Starbound Conclave

Renown comes from four kinds of work, each bounded so no one repeated deed can carry you: **research** (each state an entry reaches, once: 1, 2, 5, 10), **commissions** (each once a week, worth less each time, nothing after its third), **teaching** (someone advanced an entry by reading your notes: 3 renown, once per entry and learner, 4 per learner) and **projects** (each stage you helped, and the whole project, once).
Renown

A rank asks for renown, breadth and variety together.\
- **Aspirant**: 0 renown, 0 traditions with at least 5 renown each, 0 kinds of work; commissions up to tier 1\
- **Fellow**: 25 renown, 2 traditions with at least 5 renown each, 2 kinds of work; commissions up to tier 2; may begin projects\
- **Companion**: 80 renown, 4 traditions with at least 5 renown each, 2 kinds of work; commissions up to tier 3; may begin projects\
- **Luminary**: 160 renown, 5 traditions with at least 5 renown each, 3 kinds of work; commissions up to tier 3; may begin projects\
- **Starbound**: 260 renown, 6 traditions with at least 5 renown each, 3 kinds of work; commissions up to tier 3; may begin projects
Ranks

A member contributes something each week. A lapsed member keeps every point of renown but takes no tier II or III commission and begins no project until they contribute again; any contribution restores them. **/jugcraft concordance conclave** shows your standing, what the next rank needs and your obligation.
Obligations

Hold what a commission asks for and use a lectern, or **/jugcraft concordance conclave fulfil <commission>**; practice commissions need only the practice carried through this week. **/jugcraft concordance conclave commissions** lists them and whether each is open to you.\

- **A Gift for the Vigil** (Crimson Vigil, tier 2): bring 24 sweet berries; 8 renown, then 4, then 2; pays 3 emeralds\
- **Runework for the Archive** (Runesmiths, tier 3): work at the Artificer's Bench in the last week; 12 renown, then 6, then 3; pays 1 diamond\
- **A Dream Recorded** (Dreamwalkers, tier 3): a dream come back from in the last week; 12 renown, then 6, then 3; pays 2 ender pearls\
- **The Hex Ledger** (Hexweavers, tier 3): a curse cast in the last week; 12 renown, then 6, then 3; pays 4 emeralds\
- **The Garden Census** (Greenwardens, tier 3): a living device tended in the last week; 12 renown, then 6, then 3; pays 1 diamond
Commissions

A project to chart the starward sky from the Conclave's lenses and vigils, for one player or a whole party. Finished, it brings every contributor 30 renown and 2 diamonds.\
- **Grinding the Lenses** (8 renown each): 32 glass panes; 8 amethyst shards; a contributor who understands Celestial Attunement; 2 contributors, or contributions on 2 different days\
- **Keeping the Vigils** (10 renown each): an observation of the sky (3); a ritual completed (1); 2 contributors, or contributions on 3 different days\
- **Drawing the Chart** (12 renown each): 16 paper; 4 gold ingots; 1 compass; 3 contributors, or contributions on 3 different days
The Starward Chart

A project to gather the Concordance's learning into one archive, for one player or a whole party. Finished, it brings every contributor 30 renown and 8 experience bottles.\
- **Raising the Shelves** (8 renown each): 12 books; 32 oak planks; 2 contributors, or contributions on 2 different days\
- **The Readings** (10 renown each): a contributor who understands First Light; a contributor who understands Alembic Arts; a mixture bottled (2); 2 contributors, or contributions on 2 different days\

The Concordance Archive

From Fellow, begin a project for yourself (**/jugcraft concordance conclave project start <project> personal**) or, as your party's leader, for your party (**... party**). Your own projects take only your work; your party's take any member's. Every stage that asks for several contributors also accepts the solo way: contributions on that many different days. Together a party finishes sooner, and every member who helped shares the achievement and the reward. Sneak and use a lectern with items to give them; use it with an empty hand to present what you understand; practices count by themselves. **/jugcraft concordance conclave project** shows progress anywhere.

book.jugcraft.arcane_concordance.foundat: What this codex records, and how to begin

The Concordance is the practice of working with the Principles that run through the world. It begins with **looking closely**. Nothing in this codex teaches by being read: you learn by examining, studying and doing, and the codex records what you have learned.

Find something that holds its own light. Amethyst grows in geodes underground; glow lichen and glow berries hang in caves.\
\
**Sneak and use** a luminous specimen to examine it. Its glow is easiest to judge **in darkness**: a dark cave, or the open sky at night.
The Concordance has five stages: Initiate > Practitioner > Adept > Master > Architect. Each opens new practices; no one needs to follow every tradition.
The Concordance, its Principles and its resources

Every invocation spends **Focus**. You hold at most 20 points; one returns every 2 seconds, whatever you are doing. Focus is yours alone: no item, device or trade can store it.\
\
While you hold an instrument, your Focus shows at the bottom right of the screen.
An instrument channels invocations. Hold it in your **main hand**; the invocations you have understood appear on the spell bar, and the first is cast with the use key.

The spell bar lists your invocations in order. The **use key** casts the first; the number keys **2**, **3** and on cast the ones after it. While the instrument is in your hand those number keys cast instead of changing the hotbar slot: scroll to change slot, or bind Spell Engine's own spell keys in Controls to free them.
Everything you know and everything in your way, in one place

Press **J** (Controls: Concordance Journal) to open your journal. It shows what the server knows of your work: your Focus and stage, every research entry you have met and what its next state asks, each route to the next stage and what it still needs, and, once you know their traditions, your Vitae, the sky's forecast, your workers, deliveries, relics, the curses and wards on you, your Conclave standing, your spires and your Prima Materia.

Each line says in words where you stand and what to do next. **Exact values** (in the journal, or in the Concordance settings) add the figures behind them: how many of what each way needs, limits and caps. The same reports print in chat with **/jugcraft concordance status**, **stage**, **spire** and the other Concordance commands.

**Left**, **Right** or the section buttons change section; **Up**, **Down**, **Page Up** and **Page Down** scroll; **R** asks for the journal again; **X** shows or hides exact values; **Tab** moves between buttons; **Esc** closes it. With GuiLib installed the journal opens as a full workspace; without it, or with **Simple journal** chosen in the settings, it opens as a plain screen showing the same.
The ten Principles and the seven resources

- **Radiance**: light, revelation and sight\
- **Ember**: heat, combustion and change by fire\
- **Rime**: cold, stillness and preservation\
- **Tempest**: storm, charge and sudden motion\
- **Strata**: stone, structure and weight\
- **Verdance**: growth, life and renewal\
- **Tide**: flow, solution and exchange\
- **Tether**: binding, sympathy and agreements\
- **Echo**: memory, sound, dreams and knowledge\
- **Hollow**: absence, decay and endings

- **Focus** (personal attention)\
- **Ley Charge** (operational energy)\
- **Principle Essence** (material value)\
- **Vitae** (biological expenditure)\
- **Astral Resonance** (celestial alignment)\
- **Bound Will** (supernatural identity)\
- **Prima Materia** (equivalence value)\
\
Nothing turns one into another except a recipe that names both, with its loss.

Knowledge is not a resource. A research entry moves through four states, **Encountered**, **Observed**, **Understood** and **Mastered**, from evidence you gather yourself. Repeating the same observation adds nothing.
**Use** a blank sheet to write down every research entry you have begun, as far as you have come (up to understood). Anyone else can **use** your notes to read them; reading does not use them up.

Notes are a shared record, not experience. Where an entry accepts notes, reading them can stand in for one way of understanding it, but you must still encounter and observe it **yourself**, and mastery comes only from your own practice. Notes from the same writer count once, and your own notes teach you nothing new.
What the Concordance shows, and what it means

When something happens, the Concordance shows it where it happened, and only when it happened:
**Preparation**: glyphs drawn in, as a circle gathers.
**Execution**: light rising where work was done, or travelling along a real transfer: Ley Charge from a pylon to the circle it feeds, Radiance from a lantern into a pylon.
**Success**: a burst of light.

**Shortage**: grey smoke and sinking ash, with a hollow falling tone: something it needs is missing. A pylon short of charge, a missed upkeep, a formula without its ingredient, a worker that cannot go on.
**Danger**: flame and sparks thrown outwards, with a sharp rising warning: a circle's containment failing, a searing stir, a damaged spire.
Both sounds have subtitles.

A crucible's liquid stands at its real volume, in the colour of its strongest property, muddied when it is murky. A searing crucible smokes and spits. A spire shows whether it is being raised, working, lacking or damaged. A worker that lacks something waits, tapping or looking about; one held up on its way stands still. A finished circle glows until its result is taken.

The Concordance settings choose how much is drawn: **Full**, **Reduced** or **Minimal** (warnings only). Large workshops draw no more than a set amount each moment, and warnings are never hidden. **Reduced motion** keeps everything calmer.
Initiate, Practitioner, Adept, Master and Architect

The Concordance has five stages, each reached by any one of its routes once the stage before it is: they are the same stages as Jugcraft's (Discovery, Workshops, Specialization, Expeditions, Shared wonders). **/jugcraft concordance stage** shows yours and, for the next, every route and what it still needs.

Jugcraft's Discovery. Reached by any one of:\
- examine something that holds its own light

Jugcraft's Workshops. Reached by any one of:\
- understand First Light

Jugcraft's Specialization. Reached by any one of:\
- master two research entries\
- understand five entries in five traditions\
- understand Circle Lore and master First Light (the Adept's Attunement)

Jugcraft's Expeditions. Reached by any one of:\
- master five entries in three traditions\
- understand nine entries in seven traditions and master First Light\
- be a Luminary of the Starbound Conclave and master two entries

Jugcraft's Shared wonders. Reached by any one of:\
- be Starbound, help finish a Conclave project and master six entries\
- raise a Concord Spire, or help raise one
The Greenwardens' practice: habitats, cultivation and living devices
A producer, a consumer, a sensor and a collector

Set on a bed, it beats every 10 seconds: in its niche it spends 1 nutrient and makes 2 Verdance (1 while a factor is merely tolerable), up to 64. Beside a Ley Pylon it pours in, 3 Verdance for 2 Ley Charge. Its niche: moisture at least 2 (best 4+); light at least 8 (best 12+); nutrients at least 1 (best 4+); diversity at least 2 (best 3+); disturbance at most 10 (best up to 6).

Feed it plant matter (by hand or hopper): seeds, leaves and the crops are a quarter of a nutrient, chaff, vines and cane a half, fruit and roots three quarters, bread and hay a whole one. Every 2 seconds it eats one and, for every 4 quarters, gives a nutrient to the poorest bed within 3 blocks. Nothing composted gives back what it cost to grow.

Set on a bed, it reads the habitat there as a comparator signal: use it with an empty hand to choose a factor, or use a crop on it to read how well that crop would grow (15 thriving, 8 slowly, 0 not at all).
Harvests ripe crops within 3 blocks into its 9 slots (hoppers take them out), 1 Verdance a harvest, drawn from a Verdant Heart within 4 blocks.
Five factors, and where each comes from
The Greenwardens' crops grow only in a Verdant Bed, and only once a Greenwarden has woken it (an empty hand wakes it and up to 64 beds joined to it). It holds up to 32 nutrients.

**Moisture** (0 to 7): water within four blocks, rain, a wet sprinkler or a canteen keep a bed wet; every step of growth dries it by one.\
**Light** (0 to 15): sun or lamps at the plant, as the server's light has it; never the time of day.\
**Nutrients**: what the bed holds. Growth spends them.\
**Diversity**: the different plants in the 5x5 round it, itself included.\
**Disturbance**: working magic round it.

Nutrients come only from declared sources: **Mendvetch** (fixed from the air), the **Mulch Maw** (waste, at a loss), **bone meal** (2 a dose, on a bed or a crop in it) and **fertilizer**. A broken bed loses what it held.\
\
Disturbance: circle anchor 3, ley pylon 2, crucible 2, verdant heart 2, lumen sconce, lumen mote 1, warding stone 1, amethyst cluster, budding amethyst 1.

A crop grows on random ticks (and a sprinkler's) at full pace while every factor is ideal, at half pace while some are only tolerable, and not at all while one is outside its range. Look at it (or use it with an empty hand) to see which.

- **Sunpetal**: moisture at least 2 (best 4+); light at least 11 (best 13+); nutrients at least 1 (best 3+); diversity at least 1 (best 3+); disturbance at most 5 (best up to 2). It costs 1 nutrient a step; harvested, 2 and 1 chaff.\
- **Dewmoss**: moisture at least 5 (best 7+); light at most 12 (best up to 9); nutrients at least 1 (best 2+). It costs 1 nutrient a step; harvested, 2 and 1 chaff.\
- **Gloamcap**: moisture at least 2 (best 3+); light at most 9 (best up to 6); nutrients at least 2 (best 4+); disturbance at least 1 (best 3+), at most 15 (best up to 10). It costs 2 nutrients a step; harvested, 1 and 1 chaff.\
- **Mendvetch**: moisture at least 1 (best 3+); light at least 8 (best 11+); disturbance at most 6 (best up to 3). It gives 1 a step; harvested, 1 and 1 chaff.

A ripe crop (step 3) is harvested with an empty hand, or by a Gleaner: its produce and Verdant Chaff, and it falls back to step 1 to grow again. A Mendvetch next to other crops also speeds them, as legumes do.

book.jugcraft.arcane_concordance.sky.att: The astrolabe and what it gives

It holds up to 32 resonance. Use it where you can see a risen pattern: it spends the pattern's cost and attunes you to it, and its effect is yours while the pattern stays up (at most 8 minutes; use it again to renew). Death ends an attunement.

A master may attune when nothing is up, by **recalling** the pattern they last observed: it costs the pattern's recall price and lasts 2 minutes, once each time the pattern comes round. Stored resonance is the alternative to waiting, never a way round the sky's count.
book.jugcraft.arcane_concordance.sky.cal: The sky keeps the world's own clock, the one the sun and moon follow: a day is 20 minutes, night runs from 19:00 to 05:00, and the moon goes from full to new and back every 8 days. Every player sees the same sky, and so does the world after a restart. What your screen draws (a shader's moon, your render settings) never changes what is up.

- **The Full Moon**: on the full moon's night, 19:00 to 05:00, a clear sky. Pays 4 resonance; Moonsight: you see in the dark while it is up. Attuning costs 4, recalling 12.\
- **The New Moon**: on the new moon's night, 19:00 to 05:00, any weather. Pays 4 resonance; Spring Tide: you breathe under water while it is up. Attuning costs 4, recalling 12.\
- **The Lantern Star**: every 3 days (days that leave 1 over 3), 18:00 to 20:00, a clear sky. Pays 2 resonance; Lantern Hands: you dig and work faster while it is up. Attuning costs 2, recalling 6.\
- **The Echo Comet**: every 19 days (days that leave 7 over 19), 20:00 to 04:00, a clear sky. Pays 8 resonance; Comet's Wake: you run faster while it is up. Attuning costs 6, recalling 16.\
- **The Winter Crown**: every 2 days (days that leave 1 over 2), in winter, 21:00 to 03:00, a clear sky. Pays 3 resonance; Frostmantle: fire does not burn you while it is up. Attuning costs 3, recalling 9.\
- **The Harvest Moon**: every night, in the Harvest Moon, 19:00 to 05:00, any weather. Pays 6 resonance; Feast Favour: villagers trade with you as with a hero while it is up. Attuning costs 4, recalling 12.

Use an Orrery Observatory with an empty hand, or ask with **/jugcraft concordance sky**, to read the forecast: today's day, time, moon and season, and every pattern up now or rising in the next 8 days, with when it rises, the weather it needs and the time of year it keeps to.

Some patterns keep to a time of year. The Winter Crown comes round only in Jugcraft's winter (the server's date; with seasons off, all year). The Harvest Moon pattern is the Halloween event's own Harvest Moon: it rises on the nights the event says, and never outside them.

Healing to full does not let you offer again as if fresh.

An offering's yield falls with your exhaustion: 0 to 3 points: 100%; 4 to 7 points: 50%; 8 to 11 points: 25%; at 12 no offering at all. Rounded down. book.jugcraft.arcane_concordance.wonders: The Concordance's endgame wonder: founded, raised and kept

A Concord Spire is raised round a **Spire Heart** by a **Master** of the Concordance, and works only while it is kept: supplied every day, whole, and attended by keepers who go on practising its tradition. It is founded in one of three **configurations**, each with its own research, practice, crown, upkeep and field. A spire is the world's, not the heart's: breaking the heart, leaving or a restart loses nothing, and a heart put back where it stood answers again.

Place the heart where the spire will stand. **Sneak and use** it with an empty hand to choose a configuration (it says what each needs), then **use** it to found the spire. Afterwards an empty hand shows how it stands; its keeper sneaking shares it with their party or takes it back.

A spire is raised in four phases, in order:\
1. **Foundation**: four Ley Pylons and four Warding Stones round the heart, as a Lesser Circle has them.\
2. **Shaft**: three blocks of dark stone stacked on the heart, and the configuration's practice carried through twice.\
3. **Crown**: the configuration's crown on the shaft, and the Kindling rite completed at a Lesser Circle within 12 blocks.\
4. **Kindling**: the spire's upkeep held three days in a row.

**/jugcraft concordance spire realign <configuration>** changes the configuration of the spire you keep nearest you, if you know what the new one needs. Before the Crown nothing is lost; after it, the Foundation and the Shaft stand, and the new crown, its Kindling and its days are done again.
Endgame works raised together and kept: the Concord Spire

From the Kindling on, each day the spire takes its configuration's item from the heart's store and Ley Charge from its own pylons. Put the item in by hand (use it on the heart), by hopper, or let a **courier** bring it: the heart files a request at a Courier Post within 16 blocks you may use whenever it holds less than two days' upkeep. A day without its upkeep takes nothing and the field rests until the next day that has it.

A spire answers keepers who keep practising: its configuration's practice carried through by its keeper (or, if shared, their party) at least once every 7 days. Unattended, it rests; the next practice wakes it.

The heart checks every part of the spire it has raised. If one is missing or wrong, the spire rests and says which and where; put it back and it works again at once. Nothing is lost: not its phase, not its days. The spire never breaks or replaces a block itself: its light goes only into open air and its growth only into crops. A Verdant Bed's crop it hastens grows by its own rules: its bed pays at least a nutrient a step, and a Mendvetch fixes none while hastened.

Use the heart with an empty hand, or **/jugcraft concordance spire**, for its phase and what it still needs, its upkeep and store, its field and its attendance. Jade, when installed, shows the same at a glance. **/jugcraft concordance spire abandon confirm** forgets the spire you keep nearest you; what you built stays.
Set up a Drone Tower in a few minutes, with endless power and building blocks. Everything here is in the creative inventory: search for it by name.
Lay a flat 15x15 square of chiseled stone bricks and place a Drone Tower Core in the very middle. A Drone Tower Foundation blueprint previews the finished tower (shift+scroll).
Take stacks of the Structural, Hangar, Armour and Avionics Modules and right-click the core with each, a few times over. It holds 1024 of each, enough for every tier.
Right-click the core and press UPGRADE DRONE TOWER. The core builds the command room, the landing pads and two exchanges round the field by itself.
Place it touching the Energy Exchange Port, the striped block on the west edge of the field. It gives endless power on every side, so the depot never runs low.
Place it anywhere within 48 blocks of the depot terminal, for example just off the edge of the field. Drones then get every building block they ask for, free.
Right-click the terminal with drones to link them. The Creative Drone is fast and needs no power. A tier N tower allows drones up to tier N.
Open the core and press UPGRADE again for each tier. Your drones fly every tier in until the spire is done at tier 9. For survival, craft the Field Manual (a book and a tier 1 drone).
book.jugcraft.drone_tower_manual.page.1: A Drone Tower is a depot that grows. Its drones carry blocks and build for you, and every tier you add holds more drones and stronger ones. Turn the pages to set one up.
book.jugcraft.drone_tower_manual.page.10: Your drones build blueprints up to 250 chunks from the tower, wherever the site's chunks are loaded; the tower keeps itself loaded. You can build more towers, each over 250 chunks from your others.
book.jugcraft.drone_tower_manual.page.11: The terminal's mode (Personal or Party) decides who may use it. Place other blueprints and your drones build those too. The tower is lit, so mobs do not spawn on it.
book.jugcraft.drone_tower_manual.page.2: Print a Drone Tower Foundation blueprint at a Blueprint Table. Hold it and shift+scroll to see how big the finished tower gets: over 200 blocks tall on a 39x39 field. Leave room.
book.jugcraft.drone_tower_manual.page.3: Lay a flat 15x15 square of chiseled stone bricks. Craft a Drone Tower Core (aluminium plates, a processor, advanced circuits and a Drone Depot Terminal) and put it in the very middle.
book.jugcraft.drone_tower_manual.page.4: Tiers are built from Structural, Hangar, Armour and Avionics Modules. Right-click the core holding them, or feed them in with pipes or conveyors. Right-click the core to see what the next tier needs.
book.jugcraft.drone_tower_manual.page.5: Press UPGRADE DRONE TOWER. The core builds tier 1 itself: eight landing pads, the command room with the depot terminal, and two exchanges on the edges of the field.
book.jugcraft.drone_tower_manual.page.6: The Energy Exchange stands on the west edge. Run cables or put generators against its Energy Exchange Port (the striped block). That powers every drone; low power only slows them.
book.jugcraft.drone_tower_manual.page.7: The Storage Exchange stands on the east edge. Pipes, conveyors and hoppers against its Cargo Exchange Port fill the depot's store, and drones take the blocks for every job from there.
book.jugcraft.drone_tower_manual.page.8: Right-click the terminal or a landing pad with a drone to link it. A tier N tower allows drones up to tier N. Tier 1 holds 32 drones; a finished tower holds 133.
book.jugcraft.drone_tower_manual.page.9: Load the next tier's modules and press UPGRADE again. From tier 2 on, your drones fly each tier in, from the bottom up, as long as power and blocks keep coming.

message.jugcraft.town.welcome: Welcome to the town! Here are %s Jugs to start you off. Spend them at the market.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.banker: You hold %s Jugs. Use a Jug Teller to send Jugs to another player.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.decorator.aut: Pumpkins, hay and orange banners. Perfect.
I've carried more pumpkins this week than a farmer.
Autumn's easy: if it's orange, it goes up.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.decorator.dec: That tree took me all morning. Worth it.
Red and white awnings, like peppermint.
Presents under the tree are just wool. Shh.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.decorator.hal: Soul lanterns on every post. Spooky!
Black and orange stripes for the stalls. Mwahaha.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.decorator.har: The feast table's set, hay's stacked, pumpkins polished.
Brown and gold for the Harvest Feast.
Carrying a whole cake across the square is harder than it looks.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.decorator.spr: Out with the old, in with the tulips!
Pink and white for the stalls this spring. What do you think?
Every window box gets fresh flowers. Every single one.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.decorator.sum: Yellow banners for summer. Sunny, like me.
The flower bed in the square was my idea.
Lanterns stay, everything else goes bright.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.decorator.win: Snow blocks for the planters, spruce for the windows.
White and pale blue. Very wintry.
Dark comes early now. I'll be watching.
Seen a creeper skulking by the east gate. Not anymore.
The town's safe. You have my word.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.guard.decembe: A guard's December: lanterns, snow and no surprises.
Somebody keeps putting tinsel on my helmet.
The tree in the square is under my protection.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.guard.hallowe: Skeletons in costume are still skeletons. I check.
The decorations are fake. The zombies aren't.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.guard.harvest: Even guards get a slice of pie at the Feast.
Guarding the pie table is a serious duty.
All quiet at the gate. Just bees.
Keep your blade sheathed in town, traveller.
Long watch in the sun. Still, nothing gets past me.
Monsters don't like the lamps. Neither do I, in this heat.
Move along, the square's that way.
Frozen solid on the wall walk. Still standing.
Snow hides footprints. Not from me.
Stay inside the walls after dark.
Harvest time! The General Store is buying.
The council has approved more pumpkins.
Enjoy our town, and spend your Jugs.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.mayor.decembe: Season's greetings from the town council!
The great tree was approved unanimously.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.mayor.hallowe: The council regrets nothing about the decorations.
Trick or treat? The mayor has neither.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.mayor.harvest: Eat, drink and buy something at the stalls.
A bountiful year for the town.
Welcome to our town! Mind the flower boxes.
The town council approves of spring.
Our walls keep the town as it ever was.
A fine summer for trade. Visit the market!
The Jug Teller in the bank keeps your Jugs safe.
Our shops buy fair and sell fair. I insist.
The town stands firm, winter or no.
The snowman has been elected to the council.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.priest.autumn: We give thanks for the harvest.
The days grow short; the candles burn longer.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.priest.decemb: The longest nights bring the brightest lights.
Goodwill to all who pass the gates.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.priest.hallow: Fear not the lanterns. They are only pumpkins.
Peace be with you, and with your costume.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.priest.harves: Share what you have; that is the feast.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.priest.spring: Spring brings new life. Welcome to the church.
The bells ring for every season.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.priest.summer: The rose window shines brightest in summer.
Rest awhile in the cool of the nave.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.priest.winter: Even in winter, the doors are open.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.townsfolk.aut: The leaves are turning gold outside the walls. Worth a walk.
Pumpkins in every window box! Autumn's my favourite.
Bring your harvest to the General Store; they pay fair Jugs.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.townsfolk.dec: Have you seen the great tree in the square? The baubles glow!
Red and green banners on every house. Merry December!
I've wrapped my presents in wool. Is that normal?
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.townsfolk.hal: Did you see the soul lanterns? Gives me the shivers.
I'm going as a pumpkin this year. Again.
The pile of jack o'lanterns in the square glows all night!
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.townsfolk.har: The Harvest Feast! The table in the square is groaning with food.
Give thanks and share the pie, that's what my gran said.
Hay bales everywhere. Mind you don't sneeze.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.townsfolk.spr: The tulips came up early this year. Lovely, aren't they?
Fresh air and new leaves. The whole town smells of blossom.
Mind the puddles by the fountain, the spring rains have been generous.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.townsfolk.sum: Warm days and long evenings. Best time to sit by the fountain.
The market's busy in summer. Have you seen the flower stall?
Keep to the shade at midday, friend.
message.jugcraft.townsfolk.townsfolk.win: Cold enough to freeze the fountain! Well, nearly.
Wrap up warm. The wind comes straight down the main street.
The snowman in the square has better posture than me.

spell.jugcraft.aegis.description: Defense. Wraps you in a shell of dawn light that absorbs the next blows. Costs 5 Focus (4 once First Light is mastered).
spell.jugcraft.aegis.name: Dawn Aegis
spell.jugcraft.cinderbolt.description: Damage. A burning shard: fire damage to the first creature it meets, which then smoulders. Stronger with fire Spell Power. Costs 5 Focus (4 once Hearthbinding is mastered).
spell.jugcraft.cinderbolt.name: Cinderbolt
spell.jugcraft.composed.description: The spell inscribed on this instrument (see the codex, Composition). Its cost and cooldown are its own.
spell.jugcraft.composed.name: Inscribed Spell
spell.jugcraft.flashstep.description: Movement. Carries you a few blocks the way you face, in a flash. Costs 4 Focus (3 once First Light is mastered).
spell.jugcraft.flashstep.name: Flashstep
spell.jugcraft.hearthflare.description: Damage. A burst of fire round you: fire damage to the nearest creatures, which then smoulder. Never you; stronger with fire Spell Power. Costs 7 Focus (6 once Hearthbinding is mastered).
spell.jugcraft.hearthflare.name: Hearthflare
spell.jugcraft.hearthguard.description: Defense. Banks the fire round you: Fire Resistance for 30 seconds. Costs 5 Focus (4 once Hearthbinding is mastered).
spell.jugcraft.hearthguard.name: Hearthguard
spell.jugcraft.hearthspark.description: Utility. A spark that kindles the unlit campfire, candle or candle cake you look at, up to 16 blocks away. Costs 3 Focus (2 once Hearthbinding is mastered).
spell.jugcraft.hearthspark.name: Hearthspark
spell.jugcraft.kindle.description: Utility. Sets a mote of steady light in the open block where you look, up to 16 blocks away, for 60 seconds. Costs 4 Focus (3 once First Light is mastered).
spell.jugcraft.kindle.name: Kindle
spell.jugcraft.lance.description: Damage. A narrow beam of light: arcane damage to the first creature it meets, stronger with arcane Spell Power. Costs 5 Focus (4 once First Light is mastered).
spell.jugcraft.lance.name: Lance of Dawn
spell.jugcraft.lanternward.description: Support. Mends you and the members of your party round you, and wards them with light. Costs 7 Focus (6 once First Light is mastered).
spell.jugcraft.lanternward.name: Lanternward
spell.jugcraft.revelation.description: Investigation. Makes the creatures round you glow, seen through walls. Costs 3 Focus (2 once First Light is mastered).
spell.jugcraft.revelation.name: Revelation

tooltip.jugcraft.adept_wand: A second instrument, attuned in a circle: it holds larger spells than an Initiate's Wand. Hold it in the main hand to cast.
tooltip.jugcraft.ammo_hoist: Stack hoists into a shaft: anything put into one climbs to the top, which hands it to the container above or beside it. Use one with an item in hand to load it.
tooltip.jugcraft.ammonium_perchlorate: The oxidizer in solid rocket fuel.
tooltip.jugcraft.amphibian_boot: Worn on your feet: you swim faster, and your air lasts about twice as long.
tooltip.jugcraft.angelheart_vial: Worn as a charm: a blow that would kill you leaves you on 2 hearts, healing for 5 seconds. The vial is used up.
tooltip.jugcraft.angelic_feather: Worn as a charm: a fall's harm comes from your food instead of your health while your food bar can pay, 0.5 food a point, and you jump a little higher.
tooltip.jugcraft.antidote: Clears poison, wither and every other harmful effect, and keeps the good ones.
tooltip.jugcraft.armoured_walker: A heavily armoured walker with a hull cannon and a piston ram. Walk with the movement keys, hold use to fire the cannon (Heavy Shells) and press attack to ram. Refuel with a diesel or kerosene bucket.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.arbalest: A crossbow with a metal prod: its bolts fly faster and hit harder.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.arbalest.stats: Bolts fly %s%% faster and hit %s%% harder than a crossbow's.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.art.chain_lash: Use: throw the weighted chain at the first foe in line, up to 9 blocks off, haul it in and reap it. Ready again after 6 s.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.art.crescent: Use: loose a crescent wave that runs ahead, through every foe in its way, until it meets a wall. Ready again after 7 s.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.art.cyclone: Use: spin three times, cutting every foe about you each time round and drawing them in. Ready again after 6 s.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.art.flurry: Use: five quick jabs at the foe ahead, too fast to be shrugged off, then a driving finish. Ready again after 5 s.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.art.iaido: Use: dash ahead; every foe you pass is cut a moment later, as the blade comes round. Ready again after 8 s.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.art.leap_slam: Use: leap and bring the hammer down where you land: harder at the centre, and harder the further you came down. Ready again after 10 s.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.art.seven_cuts: Use: seven cuts in a breath, each across every foe ahead, leaving arcs in the air. Ready again after 6 s.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.battle_axe: Chops wood like an axe and breaks a shield's guard for 5 seconds.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.battleblade: A great saw-backed cleaver: each hit wears every piece of the foe's armor.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.bill: A hooked polearm: pulls the foes it strikes towards you and drags riders from the saddle.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.boon.drain: Each hit heals you half a heart.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.boon.ember: A hit sets the foe alight (3 s).
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.boon.frost: A hit chills the foe, slowing it (Slowness II, 3 s).
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.boon.gale: A hit throws the foe up and back.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.boon.harvest: A kill heals you two hearts (once every 5 s), and every fifth kill charges your next blow to loose a pale crescent.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.boon.howl: A hit cows the foe, weakening its blows (Weakness, 3 s).
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.boon.mark: A hit makes the foe glow, seen through walls (4 s).
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.boon.shock: A hit arcs to the nearest other foe within 4 blocks, for 30% of the blow.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.boon.stitch: Three hits on one foe within 4 s stitch it, slowing it (Slowness II, 2 s).
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.boon.tide: 25% harder against a foe in water or rain.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.boon.venom: A hit poisons the foe (Poison, 4 s).
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.boon.wither: A hit withers the foe (Wither, 3 s).
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.brazier_mace: A mace whose head is a burning brazier: sets foes alight. Use it to light a campfire, a candle or the ground.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.chakram: A bladed ring, held by its wrapped rim: quick slicing cuts.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.dagger: Quick stabs at a short reach. A blow from behind deals half again as much.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.earthbreaker: A siege hammer. Knocks foes back and breaks a shield's guard for 5 seconds.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.estoc: Thrusts through mail: more damage the more armor the foe wears.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.executioner: Half again as much damage to a foe at or below 30% of its health.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.flail: A hit dazes the foe, slowing it for 2 seconds.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.flanged_mace: Breaks a shield's guard for 3 seconds.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.francisca: A throwing axe with an upswept bit. Chops wood like an axe.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.glaive: A blade on a pole: sweeps at a long reach.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.greatsword: Slow, heavy sweeps with a long reach. Staggers shields.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.halberd: Thrusts through every foe in line, at a long reach. Breaks a shield's guard for 3 seconds.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.harpoon: A barbed spear on a line: stabs in the hand.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.heater_shield: A light shield, quick to raise.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.javelin: A light spear made for throwing: quick jabs in the hand.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.kama: Quick hooking cuts. Use on grass, ferns, vines or leaves to cut all of them about it, 3 by 3 by 3.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.katana: A curved single-edged blade, drawn and cut in one motion: quick, clean cuts.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.katar: A punching blade, gripped across its frame: quick straight jabs at a short reach.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.kusarigama: A sickle on a weighted chain: quick hooking cuts.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.labrys: A double-bitted axe. Its finishing blow whirls right round, striking every foe about you.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.lance: A horseman's charge: hits harder and unhorses riders. Long reach, slow jabs.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.line.bonecarved: Made of what death leaves; strikes the undead harder.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.line.ironclad: Plated, painted and bolted; wears half as fast.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.line.runebound: Its runes glow, and mark what it strikes.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.line.vesperine.tra: Trophy of Vesperine, the Last Reaper
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.longbow: A tall bow: slower to draw than a bow, but its arrows fly faster and hit harder.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.longbow.stats: Full draw in %s s. Arrows fly %s%% faster than a bow's.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.longsword: Use to parry: blocks 60% of the damage from in front.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.maul: The heaviest blow. Its finishing blow shakes the ground, staggering every foe close by.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.moonblade: A crescent-bladed greatsword: broad, sweeping cuts.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.nodachi: A great curved sword, drawn and swung with both hands at a long reach.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.pike: The longest reach, but nothing nearer than 2 blocks. Half again as much damage to riders and mounts.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.quarterstaff: Knocks foes back. Use to parry: blocks 50% of the damage from in front.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.rapier: Quick thrusts. Use to parry: blocks 35% of the damage from in front.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.sabre: A horseman's blade: quick sweeping cuts, 3 more damage from the saddle.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.scythe: Wide sweeps at a long reach. Use on ripe crops to reap them, 3 by 3, and replant.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.spear: Jab, or hold use to charge with it.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.star_shield: A four-pointed star of gold, quick to raise as a heater shield is.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.throw.chakram: Hold use, then let go to throw it: %s damage. It flies flat, cuts every foe on its way out and back, and returns to your hand.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.throw.francisca: Hold use, then let go to throw it: %s damage. It tumbles end over end and breaks a raised shield's guard for 3 seconds.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.throw.harpoon: Hold use, then let go to throw it: %s damage. It keeps its speed underwater and hauls what it strikes towards you.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.throw.javelin: Hold use, then let go to throw it: %s damage. It flies far and straight.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.tower_shield: A great shield that covers your flanks and braces you against blows; heavy to carry and slow to raise.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.twinblade: A blade at each end of the grip: quick cuts, turn and turn about.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.two_handed: The blow lands as the swing comes round, on every foe in its arc.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.war_fork: A barbed fork set against a charge: half again as much damage to a foe coming at you.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.war_hammer: Knocks foes back and breaks a shield's guard for 5 seconds.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.war_pick: A beaked war pick that mines stone and ore as its metal's pickaxe does.
tooltip.jugcraft.arms.zweihander: The widest cleave. Use to guard: blocks 50% of the damage from in front.
tooltip.jugcraft.artificer_bench: Use with 4 ingots (1 netherite): forge a ring. Use with a ring: enhance it (the codex lists how).
tooltip.jugcraft.assay_glass: Use it on an Alembic Crucible to measure every property, pending and dissolved. In a master's hands it also says what a dose would do, and why.
tooltip.jugcraft.assayers_scale: Use with a material to weigh it, and again to dissolve it into grains; with an empty hand and a material in your other hand, to form one more of it
tooltip.jugcraft.astrolabe: Draw resonance from an observatory; use it under a risen pattern to attune to it.
tooltip.jugcraft.aura_candle.muddled: Its scents clash: it gives light, but no aura
tooltip.jugcraft.barbed_wire: Slows and cuts whatever pushes through it. Sneak to pick your way across slowly but unhurt.
tooltip.jugcraft.bastion_autocannon: Twin quick-firing cannon for a 3x3 tower top. Hold attack to fire Flak Shells that burst beside anything flying.
tooltip.jugcraft.bastion_concrete: Board-marked cast concrete: tougher than plain concrete against blasts. Also makes walls.
tooltip.jugcraft.bastion_embrasure: Bastion concrete with a narrow gun slit through it, to see and shoot out through.
tooltip.jugcraft.bastion_mortar: A compact heavy mortar for a 3x3 tower top. Climb aboard and press attack to lob a Heavy Shell at your marked target, or where you look.
tooltip.jugcraft.bastion_parapet: A crenellated top for a gun deck: two merlons with a gap to shoot through.
tooltip.jugcraft.bastion_parapet_corner: A parapet's corner: one big merlon to turn a ring of parapets round a corner.
tooltip.jugcraft.blast_door: A heavy steel door that only redstone opens. As blast-proof as blast-proof concrete.
tooltip.jugcraft.bonding_charm: Use: bind a Hearthling, or call yours to you. Sneak: release it.
tooltip.jugcraft.bonecarvers_pattern: A smithing template: carves a steel dagger, flail, glaive or labrys in bone, with a bone block.
tooltip.jugcraft.booster_rail: Powered by redstone and loaded with solid propellant (8 boosts each), it kicks a passing minecart to full speed and keeps it there for 10 seconds, uphill too.
tooltip.jugcraft.broom.how: Look where you want to go: forward flies, back brakes, jump climbs
tooltip.jugcraft.bunker_bunk: Two bunks one above the other. Use it to sit on the lower bunk. It sets no spawn point.
tooltip.jugcraft.bunker_door: A heavy strapped timber door for dugouts and bunkers. Opens by hand.
tooltip.jugcraft.bunker_lamp: A caged lamp: hang it from a ceiling or stand it on a floor.
tooltip.jugcraft.candy_tray.burnt_sugar: Burnt. Use it to chip it off the tray
tooltip.jugcraft.candy_tray.candy_corn: Pour more candy corn on for another band of colour, then use it to break it up

tooltip.jugcraft.candy_tray.cream_carame: Use it to cut it up once it has set

tooltip.jugcraft.candy_tray.fudge: Use it to cut it up once it has set
tooltip.jugcraft.candy_tray.hard_candy: Break it up with sticks in your other hand for lollipops

tooltip.jugcraft.candy_tray.salt_water_t: Hold use to pull it while it's warm, or it sets hard
tooltip.jugcraft.candy_tray.toffee: Use it to break it up once it has set

tooltip.jugcraft.capacity_module: Holds its base charge again (up to 2)
tooltip.jugcraft.cement: Use on construction foam to set it into concrete. Mix with gravel and water to make concrete.
tooltip.jugcraft.chainsaw: Fells whole trees (sneak to cut one log)
tooltip.jugcraft.check_source: A weak sealed source for testing a Geiger counter
tooltip.jugcraft.chisel: Use on a headstone to cut its epitaph
tooltip.jugcraft.chlorine_grenade: Bursts into a cloud of chlorine that hurts whatever breathes inside it for 10 seconds, through armor. Fish and the undead don't breathe.
tooltip.jugcraft.cider_barrel.servings: Holds %s of %s servings of cider (still ageing)

tooltip.jugcraft.clockwork_porter: Use on a block: unfold a porter. Give it a route with a Porter Key.
tooltip.jugcraft.cloud_seeding_rocket: Fire it into the sky to bring rain for five minutes. Weather rockets share a two-minute cooldown.

tooltip.jugcraft.concordance.binding_spe: Something that binds: sneak and use to examine it
tooltip.jugcraft.concordance.celestial_s: Instrument of the sky: sneak and use to examine it

tooltip.jugcraft.concordance.crimson_spe: Crimson specimen: sneak and use to examine it
tooltip.jugcraft.concordance.dream_speci: Dreamlike: sneak and use to examine it
tooltip.jugcraft.concordance.garden_spec: Living specimen: sneak and use to examine it

tooltip.jugcraft.concordance.jade.dorman: Dormant: a Greenwarden must wake it

tooltip.jugcraft.concordance.jade.spire_: Not founded: sneak and use it to choose a configuration, then use it to found one
tooltip.jugcraft.concordance.relic_speci: Something old: sneak and use to examine it
tooltip.jugcraft.concordance.specimen: Luminous specimen: sneak and use to examine it
tooltip.jugcraft.concordance.sympathy_sp: A likeness: sneak and use to examine it
tooltip.jugcraft.construction_foam: Light and quick to break. Use cement on it to set it into concrete.
tooltip.jugcraft.control_remote.unbound: Not bound: use it on a logic controller
tooltip.jugcraft.corrugated_iron: Galvanised sheet for bunker roofs and trench walls.
tooltip.jugcraft.courier_post: Use with an item: request a stack of exactly it. Empty hand: its history. Porters bound by a Porter Key fetch.
tooltip.jugcraft.crimson_chalice: Use: offer health for Vitae. Sneak: a Crimson Surge. With a Thornheart Blade in the other hand: feed it.
tooltip.jugcraft.cursed_spindle: Used on a Spinning Wheel at night: prick your finger, and wake in the Spindle Loft
tooltip.jugcraft.death_knell: Rung at a grave at night, among lit candles, with a wreath laid on it

tooltip.jugcraft.dewmoss: Plant it in a Verdant Bed in the shade; harvested, full of Tide.
tooltip.jugcraft.diesel_walker: A diesel mech with a drill arm and a big fist. Walk with the movement keys, jump with jump, hold use to drill and attack to punch. Refuel with a diesel or kerosene bucket.
tooltip.jugcraft.dreamglass: Brought back from a dream. Ward sigils are made with it.
tooltip.jugcraft.duckboard: A slatted walkway to keep boots out of the mud.
tooltip.jugcraft.earthbinding_template: A smithing template. With a gold ingot it binds a thallite helmet, chestplate, leggings or boots into Earthbound armor, for good. Keeps enchantments and wear.
tooltip.jugcraft.earthbound_thallite_boo: Earthbound: thallite bound with gold. Protects as thallite armor does.
tooltip.jugcraft.earthbound_thallite_che: Earthbound: thallite bound with gold. Protects as thallite armor does.
tooltip.jugcraft.earthbound_thallite_hel: Earthbound: thallite bound with gold. Protects as thallite armor does.
tooltip.jugcraft.earthbound_thallite_leg: Earthbound: thallite bound with gold. Protects as thallite armor does.
tooltip.jugcraft.enriched_uranium_cylind: Low-enriched uranium hexafluoride, ready for the Fuel Fabricator
tooltip.jugcraft.exosuit_boots: No fall damage, and steps up a full block (1 JE/t)
tooltip.jugcraft.exosuit_chestplate: Energy shield: regrows up to 4 hearts of absorption (4,000 JE per half heart). Hold jump in the air to fly, like the rocket pack
tooltip.jugcraft.exosuit_helmet: Night vision in the dark (2 JE/t while dark)
tooltip.jugcraft.field_kitchen: A stove for a Cooking Pot on top. Burns logs, coal, charcoal or coke, and only starts a new piece while a pot stands on it.
tooltip.jugcraft.field_telephone: Power it from behind and every telephone on its channel within 256 blocks rings and gives a signal from its front. Use a dye to set the channel.
tooltip.jugcraft.fire_bangle: Worn in a Bracelet slot: once you understand Hearthbinding, your melee blows leave the creature smouldering for 3 seconds.
tooltip.jugcraft.fire_control_table: Lays every linked gun that has nobody at its controls. Use empty-handed to change mode (hold, converge, parallel, creeping barrage, sentry), sneak to change the sector, with a Range Finder to set the target. A redstone pulse fires one round from each gun.
tooltip.jugcraft.fire_control_wire: Use on a fire control table, then on a gun nearby, to link (or unlink) it. Sneak-use on a table to cut every link.

tooltip.jugcraft.first_aid_kit: Heals four hearts. Then a 10 second wait before the next.
tooltip.jugcraft.flak_gun: Twin anti-aircraft cannon. Hold attack to fire Flak Shells that burst beside anything flying.
tooltip.jugcraft.flame_arrester: Use on an empty storage tank to re-rate it for flammable liquids
tooltip.jugcraft.flashbang: A blinding flash: players who see it are blinded, mobs lose their target and stagger. No damage.
tooltip.jugcraft.flight_plan.blank: Blank: sneak and use it on the rocket pad to deliver to
tooltip.jugcraft.foam_canister: Foam for the foam sprayer: fills 32 blocks.
tooltip.jugcraft.foam_sprayer: Sprays construction foam where you aim, filling up to 12 open blocks: bridge gaps, seal caves and hold back water or lava. Uses foam canisters from your inventory.
tooltip.jugcraft.formula: Use a blank formula on a crucible to record its process; sneak to set a written one for the crucible to repeat.
tooltip.jugcraft.fortress_rifle: A long gun for a 5x5 tower top. It throws Heavy Shells fast and flat, out to about 200 blocks.
tooltip.jugcraft.fortune_module: More ore drops, up to Fortune III (drill only; not with silk touch)
tooltip.jugcraft.frost_horn: Blown at night, standing on snow or ice: the snow opens onto the Glacier Hall
tooltip.jugcraft.gas_curtain: A wet blanket for a dugout's doorway. Let down, it keeps chlorine and smoke out; use it to roll it up or let it down. You walk through it either way.

tooltip.jugcraft.gas_mask: Keeps out chlorine and smoke, and its tinted lenses a flashbang. The filter wears in gas; repair it with charcoal.
tooltip.jugcraft.geiger_counter: Clicks faster near radiation; shows your dose rate and total dose
tooltip.jugcraft.gilders_pattern: A smithing template: gilds a steel longsword, rapier, sabre or halberd with a gold ingot.
tooltip.jugcraft.gleaner: Harvests ripe crops round it for a Verdance each, drawn from a Verdant Heart nearby.
tooltip.jugcraft.gloamcap: Plant it in a Verdant Bed in the dark near working magic.
tooltip.jugcraft.golden_thimble: In the offhand, turns aside the first projectile every 15 seconds
tooltip.jugcraft.gossamer_silk: Madame Tatterlace's silk: unpicks into string, and spins a cheaper Cursed Spindle

tooltip.jugcraft.grenade: Bursts where it lands, hurting living things nearby. Never breaks blocks.

tooltip.jugcraft.guns.baffled_silencer: Brass baffles in a long can: quieter still, and nothing lost.

tooltip.jugcraft.guns.beam_pistol: A ray pistol held in one hand: its beam passes through every creature in its line. Breaks open to load. Runs on Energy Cells.
tooltip.jugcraft.guns.bellmouth: A flintlock blunderbuss with a flared muzzle. Ten balls a shot at close range, then a long reload. Fires paper cartridges.
tooltip.jugcraft.guns.breacher: A pump shotgun fed from a box magazine, so quick to reload. Fires buckshot shells.
tooltip.jugcraft.guns.bronco_smg: A short submachine gun with a broad barrel shroud, fired in one hand: it bucks hard. Hold to fire. Fires light rounds.
tooltip.jugcraft.guns.buckshot_shell: A paper shell of lead shot over a brass head.
tooltip.jugcraft.guns.bulldog_pistol: A one-handed hand cannon that breaks open to load its one heavy round. Fires rifle rounds.
tooltip.jugcraft.guns.bullfrog: A stubby grenade launcher with a sliding barrel, loaded a grenade at a time. Each shot lobs it to go off where it lands; it never breaks a block. Loads any grenade, the one in the other hand first.
tooltip.jugcraft.guns.caisson_pistol: A pressure pistol held in one hand: its bolt leaps from its mark to two more creatures close by. The tall tank on top is changed to reload. Runs on Energy Cells.
tooltip.jugcraft.guns.charge: Each round: %s JE from your Energy Cells
tooltip.jugcraft.guns.cinder_repeater: A Nether-forged repeater, firing for as long as the trigger is held; its shots set what they hit alight. Fires light rounds.
tooltip.jugcraft.guns.coach_gun: An over-and-under shotgun that breaks open to load. Eight pellets a shot, two barrels. Fires buckshot shells.

tooltip.jugcraft.guns.diamond_bayonet: A diamond blade under the muzzle. Stab with it up close.
tooltip.jugcraft.guns.drover_rifle: A lever-action rifle with a long tube, worked between shots and loaded a round at a time. Fires rifle rounds.

tooltip.jugcraft.guns.energy_cell: Charge for the energy guns. Fill it at a Charging Station; a reload draws on it and leaves it.
tooltip.jugcraft.guns.extended_barrel: A longer barrel: reaches farther and strays less.
tooltip.jugcraft.guns.extended_magazine: Half as many rounds again, a little slower to change.
tooltip.jugcraft.guns.fitting: Fit it with the gun in a crafting grid; the gun and shears take the last off.

tooltip.jugcraft.guns.garrison_rifle: A steel assault rifle with a curved magazine, firing for as long as the trigger is held. Fires rifle rounds.
tooltip.jugcraft.guns.glowmouth: A plasma blunderbuss loaded a charge at a time: its burst leaps from the creature nearest the aim to two more close by. Runs on Energy Cells.

tooltip.jugcraft.guns.iron_bayonet: A blade under the muzzle. Stab with it up close.

tooltip.jugcraft.guns.medium_scope: A short scope: a closer view down the sights, a little clumsy from the hip.

tooltip.jugcraft.guns.muzzle_brake: Ports at the muzzle throw the blast aside: half the kick, steadier aimed.
tooltip.jugcraft.guns.netherite_bayonet: A netherite blade under the muzzle. Stab with it up close.
tooltip.jugcraft.guns.one_handed: One-handed: with one in each hand, left click fires this one, right click the other
tooltip.jugcraft.guns.paper_cartridge: A lead ball and its powder, wrapped in paper for a muzzle-loader.
tooltip.jugcraft.guns.patchwork_carbine: A stockless carbine patched from scrap. One shot each pull. Fires rifle rounds.

tooltip.jugcraft.guns.rifle_round: A brass case, a lead bullet and a full charge.
tooltip.jugcraft.guns.riveter_smg: An iron submachine gun that empties a long magazine in a hurry. Hold to fire. Fires light rounds.
tooltip.jugcraft.guns.rust_midge: A copper machine pistol, scrap-built and quick. Hold to fire. Fires light rounds.
tooltip.jugcraft.guns.sapper_revolver: A short revolver whose cylinder swings out to load a round at a time. Fires light rounds.

tooltip.jugcraft.guns.silencer: A wool-packed can for the muzzle: a much quieter shot, a little weaker.

tooltip.jugcraft.guns.solenoid_rifle: A gauss rifle: the rings along its barrel throw a heavy slug through every creature in its line. Runs on Energy Cells.
tooltip.jugcraft.guns.speed_magazine: A sprung, flared magazine: changed in two thirds of the time.

tooltip.jugcraft.guns.steel_bayonet: A steel blade under the muzzle, wrapped at the grip. Stab with it up close.

tooltip.jugcraft.guns.tactical_grip: A stubby grip under the fore-end: a little steadier from the hip, and a little less kick.

tooltip.jugcraft.guns.warden_pistol: An iron service pistol with a sliding breech, held in one hand. One shot each pull. Fires light rounds.
tooltip.jugcraft.guns.weighted_stock: A heavy stock: soaks up the kick and holds the aim.
tooltip.jugcraft.guns.wooden_stock: A plain wooden stock: a little of everything.
tooltip.jugcraft.habitat_gauge: Set on a Verdant Bed: it reads the habitat there as a comparator signal. Use a crop on it to ask about that crop.
tooltip.jugcraft.hazmat: Each piece stops 22.5% of nuclear radiation (90% for the full suit)
tooltip.jugcraft.he_rocket: Rocket launcher ammunition: a big blast where it hits (12 hearts at the centre, 5 blocks across).

tooltip.jugcraft.heavy_shell: Ammunition for the Siege Mortar and the Self-Propelled Howitzer.
tooltip.jugcraft.hex.flying: Rub on for a feather-light fall
tooltip.jugcraft.hex.giant: Makes the drinker a giant, if there is room
tooltip.jugcraft.hex.shrinking: Makes the drinker half their size
tooltip.jugcraft.homing_rocket: Rocket launcher ammunition: locks on to the hostile mob nearest your crosshair within 48 blocks and steers into it. A smaller blast.

tooltip.jugcraft.illumination_flare: A white burst that makes hostile mobs within 48 blocks glow for 30 seconds.
tooltip.jugcraft.imperial_crest: The arms of no real empire: a winged cog on a crimson shield. Faces you when placed.
tooltip.jugcraft.imperial_gas_lamp: Burns with a bright, warm white flame.
tooltip.jugcraft.infernal_claws: Worn as a charm: fire's harm (not lava's) comes from your food instead of your health while your food bar can pay, 0.5 food a point.
tooltip.jugcraft.initiate_wand: A first instrument. Hold it to cast the invocations you have understood; a Concordance invocation needs a Concordance instrument in the main hand.
tooltip.jugcraft.iodine: Leached from kelp with sulfuric acid.

tooltip.jugcraft.kaiser_helmet: Kaiser: field grey and gilt, the parade dress of the Winged Cog. Protects as steel armor does.
tooltip.jugcraft.kaiser_leggings: Kaiser: field grey and gilt, the parade dress of the Winged Cog. Protects as steel armor does.

tooltip.jugcraft.kerosene_tank: A rocket casing filled with RP-1 kerosene, the fuel of a liquid rocket motor.
tooltip.jugcraft.kiln_seal: Pressed into a magma block in the Nether or a volcanic land: the magma opens onto the Cinder Kiln

tooltip.jugcraft.kraken_shell: Worn as a charm: drowning's harm comes from your food instead of your health while your food bar can pay, 0.5 food a point.

tooltip.jugcraft.leather_belt: Worn in the Belt slot: one more Charm slot. It cannot be taken off while that slot holds a charm.
tooltip.jugcraft.lesser_fire_focus: Worn in the Spell Focus slot: +2 fire Spell Power, so Cinderbolt and Hearthflare burn hotter. It holds no Focus.
tooltip.jugcraft.leu_fuel_assembly: Standard reactor fuel. A full core is 193 assemblies and runs about a day at full power
tooltip.jugcraft.line_rocket: Stand by a zipline anchor and use it while looking at another anchor up to 96 blocks away: it strings a steel line between them.
tooltip.jugcraft.livery: Smithing template: repaints exosuit pieces and the katana, keeping their charge
tooltip.jugcraft.lox_tank: A rocket casing filled with liquid oxygen, the oxidizer of a liquid rocket motor.
tooltip.jugcraft.map_table: Use it to read the target marks plotted within 256 blocks. Sneak and use it to give the next one to a fire control table within 4 blocks.
tooltip.jugcraft.mendvetch: Plant it in a Verdant Bed: it gives nutrients back to the beds round it.
tooltip.jugcraft.module_fitting: Use it on a charging station holding the tool

tooltip.jugcraft.mourning_wreath: Lay it on a grave for the Last Rites
tooltip.jugcraft.mulch_maw: Feed it plant matter: it gives the nutrients to the poorest Verdant Bed round it.

tooltip.jugcraft.nuclear.chw_pump: Pumps chilled water from the air handlers' coils through its chiller
